angularDiameterSource: Half the shadow diameter 6 sqrt(3) theta_g = 39.49 microarcseconds of a non-spinning black hole of the angular gravitational radius theta_g = 3.8 +/- 0.4 microarcseconds the EHT measured (EHT Collaboration 2019, ApJL 875, L1, M87 Paper I, Table 1; the formula from EHT Sgr A* Paper VI, arXiv:2311.09484, Section 3), at 16.8 Mpc (Paper I, Table 1).
distanceSource: EHT Collaboration (2019, ApJL 875, L1; arXiv:1906.11238), M87 Paper I, Table 1: D = 16.8 +/- 0.8 Mpc, rederived from likelihood distributions in Paper VI.
radiusSource: Radius: half the shadow diameter of a non-spinning black hole of the angular gravitational radius the EHT measured from its 2017 images, theta_g = GM/(D c^2) = 3.8 +/- 0.4 microarcseconds (EHT Collaboration 2019, ApJL 875, L1, M87 Paper I, Table 1, from Paper VI): d_sh = 6 sqrt(3) theta_g (EHT Collaboration 2022, Sgr A* Paper VI, arXiv:2311.09484, Section 3) = 39.49 microarcseconds; a spinning black hole's shadow is up to 7.5% smaller (same section). At the distance 16.8 Mpc (Paper I, Table 1): 19.745e-6 x 16.8e6 au = 331.72 au = 49,624,960,315 km at 149,597,870.7 km per au. It is the size of the dark region an observer sees, not an event horizon. GM from the mass (6.5 +/- 0.7) x 10^9 solar masses (Paper I, Table 1) times the JPL solar GM 132712440041.93938 km^3/s^2.

shape.qualification: A black sphere at the measured shadow radius: the dark region an observer sees, not an event horizon or a surface.

massSource: EHT Collaboration (2019, ApJL 875, L1; arXiv:1906.11238), M87 Paper I, Table 1: M = (6.5 +/- 0.7) x 10^9 solar masses, the average of three methods on the 2017 images (Paper VI), at D = 16.8 Mpc.
